expectations.text: Identifies the fat controller / missing service layer anti-pattern
expectations.evidence: The billing module is implemented as a single 'fat controller' — all business logic, data access, and external API orchestration lives directly inside Fastify route handlers. [...] ### 1. No Service or Domain Layer (Critical)

expectations.text: Notes that business logic (computing daysLeft, isActive, customer lookup) is embedded in route handlers
expectations.evidence: A `BillingService` (or equivalent application-layer class) that owns orchestration logic such as 'create or retrieve Stripe customer, create subscription, persist record.' [...] Any change to subscription creation logic (e.g., adding trial periods, applying coupons) requires touching route-handler code, which should be concerned only with HTTP concerns (parsing, validation, response shaping).

expectations.text: Flags direct Stripe API calls in route handlers instead of an application/infrastructure layer
expectations.evidence: Every route handler directly imports and calls `stripe.*` and `db.*`. There is no intermediate layer that encapsulates business logic. [...] ### 2. Stripe Client Instantiated as a Module-Level Singleton (High) [...] Makes it impossible to inject a mock Stripe client in tests — there is no seam.

expectations.text: Flags direct DB queries (db.select, db.update) in route handlers
expectations.evidence: Every route handler directly imports and calls `stripe.*` and `db.*`. [...] A repository or data-access layer that wraps the Drizzle queries so they can be swapped or mocked in tests. [...] await db.update(subscriptions).set({ status: 'cancelled', ... }).where(...); const [user] = await db.select().from(users).where(eq(users.id, userId));

expectations.text: Recommends extracting a BillingService (application layer) and/or BillingRepository (infrastructure layer)
expectations.evidence: Extract a `BillingRepository` — owns all Drizzle queries for `subscriptions` and `invoices`. Returns typed domain objects, not raw DB rows. Create a `BillingService` — orchestrates adapter + repository calls. Contains all business logic (create-or-get-customer, cancel-with-status-update, etc.).

expectations.text: Notes the missing composition root / dependency injection
expectations.evidence: The Stripe client is instantiated at module load time using `process.env` directly. [...] Makes it impossible to inject a mock Stripe client in tests — there is no seam. [...] Instantiate the Stripe client inside a `StripeAdapter` class that accepts the key via constructor injection (from `SecretsProvider`). Register it as a Fastify plugin/decorator so it can be overridden in tests.
